preimage_action.short_description: Restricting funds for an impaired-driving technology standard
preimage_action.compact_description: The amendment would bar the specified division’s funds from implementing the named impaired-driving standard. It would not repeal the statute or cover every federal account. The recorded amendment failed; membership remains unaccepted.
preimage_action.meaning:
The January22,2026 recorded question was adoption of PartBAmendment1 to H.R.7148, not passage of the whole appropriations package. It would insert section195 at the end of TitleIofDivisionD: none of the funds made available by this Act may be used to implement IIJAsection24220, the named advanced impaired-driving provision. The pending bill's section3 ordinarily confines this Act within a division to that division. This is a restriction on the funds made available by DivisionD, not a permanent repeal of section24220 or a restriction on every federal account. The rider does not independently cancel all vehicle-control technology, private research or every appropriation; no universal calendar sunset is invented from the package's fiscal-year title.
The complete retained section24220note, including its2022amendment, defines alternatives: passive driver-performance monitoring with prevention/limitation of operation if impairment is detected; passive accurate blood-alcohol detection with prevention/limitation if above the legal limit; OR a combination. The definition does not require both detection paths in every system. It does not itself establish that every passenger has a government-operated remote switch or that the particular technology already exists in every vehicle.
The statute directs Transportation through NHTSA to prescribe a federal motor-vehicle safety standard for new passenger vehicles manufactured after the standard's effective date. The named new/passenger-vehicle definitions remain incorporated; used vehicles are not silently brought into a universal retrofit mandate. The retained30111(a)/(b) baseline requires practicability, objective terms and vehicle-safety need, with the specified information, consultation, appropriateness and statutory-purpose considerations. The cited source is a dated statutory baseline, not proof of a current finalized technical standard or an engineering certificate for a particular vehicle.
The section's initial rulemaking clock, conditional extension and reporting duties remain distinct from manufacturer compliance. Manufacturer compliance is two to three years after rule issuance, not an immediate mandate on every existing vehicle. If the Secretary determines the standard cannot meet the specified30111requirements by the applicable date, the statute permits its bounded extension and requires the stated reports, including recurring reports and a ten-year nonfinalization report. No current final-rule status or particular deadline is certified. The congressional fatality/cost/prevention findings are attributed statutory findings, not this candidate's independent estimate or proof of realized safety benefits.
The recorded amendment was rejected164–268with4NotVoting, following the earlier voice appearance and postponed recorded vote. The funding restriction was not adopted into the package by this question, and the House vote did not itself repeal or enact the underlying law. A Yea supports adopting this exact funding restriction; a Nay opposes adopting it without establishing support for every possible sensor design, surveillance claim or technology outcome. No motive, privacy outcome, crash reduction, expenditure, equipment installation or actual implementation halt is inferred.
Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal based on direct transportation-equipment and technical-standard implementation governance under the existing criterion. A competing boundary treats this as private consumer-vehicle regulation. Independent source, whole-action and taxonomy review is required before acceptance or publication; no accepted ontology change follows.
limitations: Exact amendment versus whole package; recorded rejection overrides preliminary voice appearance and does not enact the rider.
Division-specific funding cohort, not permanent statutory repeal or every federal account; no invented universal spending-year sunset.
Passive driver-performance OR blood-alcohol detection OR combination; no forced both-path design or universal retrofit.
Practicability/objectivity, conditional timing, two-to-three-year manufacturer compliance and separate reporting remain; no current final-rule or technical-compliance finding.
Statutory findings are attributed, not independently verified safety forecasts. No actual sensor, privacy, crash, funding or implementation outcome.
Consumer-vehicle versus direct transportation/technical-system taxonomy remains an unaccepted review question.
